{{Short description|American statistician}}
'''Judith O'Fallon''', née '''Judith Rich''', is a retired American [[statistician]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.postbulletin.com/mike-and-judy-ofallon-50th-anniversary|title=Mike and Judy O'Fallon, 50th Anniversary|date=August 30, 2011|website=Rochester Post Bulletin}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.postbulletin.com/obituaries/obits/william-michael-ofallon-5ecfe7691e6ee72e56b8942b-621ce28b3fb20d75d9105dc7|title=William Michael O'Fallon|date=February 28, 2022|website=Rochester Post Bulletin}}</ref> She was elected as a [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1984,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/|title=American Statistical Association|website=American Statistical Association}}</ref> and is also a lifetime member of it.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/02/01/lifetimemembers2_14/|title=Recognizing the ASA's Lifetime Members &#124; Amstat News|date=February 1, 2014}}</ref>

==Education==
In 1973 she received a PhD in statistics from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. Her [[dissertation]] was "Discriminant Analysis Under Truncation" and her advisor was [[Norman Lloyd Johnson|N.L. Johnson]].<ref>{{cite thesis|author1=O'Fallon, Judith Rich |title=Discriminant analysis under truncation|url=https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/handle/1840.4/2666?show=full|location=North Carolina State University |degree=PhD |year=1973}}</ref><ref>[https://archive.org/download/commencement19741974univ/commencement19741974univ.pdf Annual Commencement]</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://stor.unc.edu/graduate/alumni/?wpv-wpcf-alumni-year=1973&wpv_aux_current_post_id=6119&wpv_aux_parent_post_id=6119&wpv_view_count=101 | title=Alumni – UNC Statistics & Operational Research }}</ref>

==Work==
She was president of the Eastern North American Region (ENAR) of the [[International Biometric Society]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/2533431|title=The World of Biometry|author=Billard, L.|year=1994|journal=Biometrics|volume=50|issue=4|pages=899–916|doi=10.2307/2533431|jstor=2533431 |pmid=7787005 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publichealth.pitt.edu/enar|title=ENAR Spring Meeting|website=publichealth.pitt.edu}}</ref>

She worked as a research statistician at the [[Mayo Clinic]] until she retired.<ref name="auto"/>

Her most cited papers are:
*Daumas‐Duport C, Scheithauer B, O'Fallon J, Kelly P. Grading of astrocytomas: a simple and reproducible method. Cancer. 1988 Nov 15;62(10):2152–2165. (Cited 1125 times, according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref name=GS>Google Scholar Author page, Accessed  May 18, 2022</ref>)
*Smith JS, Perry A, Borell TJ, Lee HK, O’Fallon J, Hosek SM, Kimmel D, Yates A, Burger PC, Scheithauer BW, Jenkins RB. Alterations of chromosome arms 1p and 19q as predictors of survival in oligodendrogliomas, astrocytomas, and mixed oligoastrocytomas. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2000 Feb 1;18(3):636–. (Cited 932 times, according to Google Scholar.<ref name=GS  />)
*Smith JS, Alderete B, Minn Y, Borell TJ, Perry A, Mohapatra G, Hosek SM, Kimmel D, O'Fallon J, Yates A, Feuerstein BG. Localization of common deletion regions on 1p and 19q in human gliomas and their association with histological subtype. Oncogene. 1999 Jul;18(28):4144–4152. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2000 Feb 1;18(3):636–. (Cited 423 times, according to Google Scholar.<ref name=GS  />)

==Personal life==
She married William Michael (Mike) O’Fallon on September 2, 1961. They had two sons, Liam and Sean. William died on February 19, 2022.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto"/>

She became a [[Rotary International|Rotarian]] in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.postbulletin.com/lifestyle/main-event-rotarys-reach-runs-from-local-to-worldwide|title=Main Event: Rotary's reach runs from local to worldwide|date=May 10, 2016|website=Rochester Post Bulletin}}</ref>
